extracted.intended_audience: registered eFilers; patent applicants and patent practitioners filing Corrected Application Data Sheets (ADS) via USPTO EFS-Web
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting a Corrected (Web-based) Application Data Sheet (ADS) in an existing U.S. patent application via USPTO EFS-Web, including what fields can be changed, regulatory requirements, required accompanying documents, fees, and UI behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered eFiler association requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be a registered eFiler and be associated to the Customer Number used as the correspondence address of the entered application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only registered filers can access and submit a Corrected Web-based ADS. The submitting registered eFiler must be associated with the Customer Number used as the correspondence address for the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted and prohibited application types
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrected Application Data Sheet is available only for existing applications of certain submission types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted: Utility (Nonprovisional), Reissue, and Designs. Not permitted: PCT, 371, Hague, Provisional, Reexam, Plant, and Supplemental Examination submissions. A Corrected ADS can only be submitted in an existing application filed on or after September 16, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements (37 CFR 1.33(b) and 1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Corrected Application Data Sheet must be signed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.33(b). See 37 CFR 1.4 for signature requirements and certifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant is prosecuting the application pro se, all inventors must sign unless a power of attorney has been given (e.g., Form PTO/AIA/81). If one or more applicants is a juristic entity (e.g., corporation), the form must be signed by a patent practitioner in certain circumstances. Follow MPEP 402 and the cited CFR provisions for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: All required fields must be completed in order to proceed with the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required fields are indicated with an asterisk (*). The EFS-Web interface will prevent submission if required fields are missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start-up data required (Application and Confirmation numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: To start the Corrected ADS you must enter the Application Number and Confirmation Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After entering those numbers click Continue. If there is a validation error it will be displayed at the top of the screen and next to the field in error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation error display behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Validation errors are displayed in the UI when data entry fails checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An error message is shown at the top of the screen and near the data field containing the error so you can identify and correct it before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: PALM data retrieval limitations and preservation of unchanged data
rubrics_metrics.description: On the Application Data tab, the Corrected ADS displays data retrieved from the USPTO PALM system, but not all data of record may be retrieved or displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a previous EFS Web-based ADS or uploaded PDF ADS was used, information should be in PALM. The system may only retrieve the mailing address of the first-named inventor; other inventor addresses may not appear on the web screen even if on file. Important anti-pattern: do not delete information you are not changing — deleting fields on the web screen will generate instructions to the Office to delete that information from the application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not attach an ADS PDF when using Corrected Web-based ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: If submitting a Corrected Web-based ADS, do not attach an ADS as a PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFS-Web will auto-generate a CorrectedADS.pdf; attaching another ADS PDF is not appropriate and may cause conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy Order filing prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions for applications under a Secrecy Order may not be filed electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application is subject to a secrecy order, use paper filing channels rather than EFS-Web.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor information edits and inventorship-change procedural requirements (37 CFR 1.48)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventor data of record is displayed and editable; changing order or editing names is done via the web screen, but adding or deleting inventors requires formal requests and fees under 37 CFR 1.48.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To change inventor order, enter the order numbers (each number used only once) and click Continue. If adding or deleting inventors, submit a request under 37 CFR 1.48(a) with proper fee(s); correction of inventorship after a first action on the merits may incur both a processing fee and an additional fee per 37 CFR 1.48(c). Correcting/updating an inventor name or changing order of joint inventors requires a request under 37 CFR 1.48(f) with the proper fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address change pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence Information is displayed but not editable via the Corrected ADS web interface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To change correspondence address, use private PAIR or file paper Form PTO/AIA/122 (Change of Correspondence Address).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application information specifics (title, entity status)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application Information is displayed and editable; Title of the Invention is required; entity claims are handled here with limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use special characters in the Title field. You may claim small entity status by checking the box and properly signing the Corrected Web-ADS per 37 CFR 1.27. You cannot use a Corrected Web-ADS to notify the Office that you are no longer entitled to small entity status — a properly signed written notification per 37 CFR 1.27(g)(2) is required. Micro entity status requires a proper micro entity certification form (PTO/SB/15A or PTO/SB/15B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative information does not create power of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative Information is displayed but not editable, and providing representative information in the ADS does not constitute appointment of power of attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To appoint or revoke a power of attorney, file the appropriate signed power of attorney form(s) (e.g., PTO/AIA/82, PTO/AIA/81, or PTO/AIA/80 accompanied by Form PTO/AIA/96) per 37 CFR 1.32.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic benefit / national stage claim rules and ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic benefit/National Stage data is displayed and editable; domestic benefit and national stage claims must comply with statutory/regulatory time limits and ordering requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding domestic benefit claims in a utility or plant application after the time period in 37 CFR 1.78 requires a petition to accept an unintentionally delayed benefit claim (including petition fee). Deleting a domestic benefit claim may be considered an intentional waiver. When claiming benefit of more than one prior application, start with the most recent and go back chronologically for each chain; multiple chains must each be provided chronologically. The UI supports Add/Remove, Move Up/Move Down, and drag-and-drop to reorganize benefit claim order. Note: The Corrected ADS will display internal PALM codes for relationships (e.g., CON, DIV, CIP, NST, SUB, REI, PRO); these codes are accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority claim rules (35 U.S.C. 119(b) and 37 CFR 1.55)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign Priority information entered in the ADS constitutes the claim for priority as required by statute and regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding a foreign priority claim after the regulatory time limits (e.g., after the later of four months from filing date of the instant application or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior foreign application) requires a petition to accept an unintentionally delayed foreign priority claim (including petition fee). Deleting a foreign priority claim may be treated as an intentional waiver. The ADS supports adding/removing multiple foreign priority claims. There is a field for entering a WIPO DAS access code to identify a foreign priority document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant information roles and change procedures (37 CFR 1.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant Information entries must designate an applicant role and changes to applicant identity have regulatory consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each applicant select one of: Assignee, Legal Representative under 35 U.S.C. 117, Joint Inventor, Person to whom the inventor is obligated to assign, or Person who shows sufficient proprietary interest. If changing the applicant, submit a request in compliance with 37 CFR 1.46(c)(2) (which includes compliance with 37 CFR 3.71 and 3.73). If correcting or updating an applicant name, submit a request under 37 CFR 1.46(c)(1); failure to specify that a change is a correction may lead the Office to treat it as a change in applicant requiring additional statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee information for publication (37 CFR 1.215(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignee information can be included if desired for the patent application publication and is editable in the ADS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the Assignee Information section only if you want assignee information included on the patent application publication. An assignee-applicant identified in Applicant Information will appear as an applicant on publication. You can Add/Remove assignees and change their order by entering order numbers (each number used only once). See the ADS instruction document referenced for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and proceeding to next screen
rubrics_metrics.description: After signing the ADS per regulatory requirements, the filer proceeds to the next screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once you have signed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.33(b) (and 1.4 as applicable), select Continue to proceed to Attach Documents. Failure to properly sign may invalidate entity claims or other certifications on the ADS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auto-generated CorrectedADS.pdf is mandatory and immutable in the submission
rubrics_metrics.description: EFS-Web will automatically generate a CorrectedADS.pdf of the web-entered data; the generated PDF cannot be removed from the Attach Documents screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may preview the CorrectedADS.pdf via a hyperlink. If you need to change the content, go back to the Application Data screen, make changes, and click Continue to regenerate the PDF. To remove the auto-generated PDF from the submission you must cancel the filing entirely. The corrected ADS will show insertions as underlining and deletions as strike-through per 37 CFR 1.76(c)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed accompanying document types with a Corrected ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain document types/descriptions may be uploaded along with a Corrected ADS filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted descriptions include, for example: Request under Rule 48 correcting inventorship (R48.REQ), Oath or Declaration filed (OATH), Miscellaneous Incoming Letter (LET.), Assignee showing of ownership per 37 CFR 3.73 (R3.73), Transmittal Letter (TRAN.LET), Petition for review by the Office of Petitions (PET.OP), Petition for review by the PCT legal office (PET.PCT), Request for Corrected Filing Receipt (CFILE), Interim Copy of Foreign Priority Document (FRPR.IC) in PDF or TXT. If no additional PDFs are required, proceed to Review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Documents behavior (CorrectedADS.pdf cannot be removed)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the Review Documents screen the CorrectedADS.pdf is present and cannot be removed from the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need to remove the CorrectedADS.pdf you must cancel the filing; otherwise proceed to calculate fees and submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee calculation and available fee types
rubrics_metrics.description: EFS-Web provides a Calculate Fees screen where filers select entity status and applicable fee codes for the Corrected ADS filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available fees for Corrected ADS filings include: Processing Fee (except provisional applications), Correction of inventorship after first action on the merits, Petition for delayed submission of a priority or benefit claim or to restore the right of priority/benefit. Adjust fee codes/amounts on the screen as appropriate for your submission and entity status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save for Later feature for Registered eFilers
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered eFilers may save an in-progress Corrected ADS submission for later completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All required ADS fields on the Application Data tab must be completed to save. Use the Save for Later button on the Confirm & Submit screen. A saved submission is not officially filed until Submit is executed; the system displays a notice and saves the submission for up to 7 days. After saving, you can view saved submission details and then resume to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS-Web session timeout warning
rubrics_metrics.description: EFS-Web sessions will time-out after one hour of inactivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A web-based ADS not submitted or saved after one hour of inactivity will be lost; you will need to log in again and re-enter information. Use Save for Later to avoid losing work.
